what: Parse Raw Person Names into Structured Components
title: Parse Raw Person Names into Structured Components
text: R package convert raw text version individual’s name structured format. functions attempt disambiguate proper name ordering (first, middle, last), parse prefixes suffixes, assign gender based upon first names.

title: Parse Raw Person Names into Structured Components
Parse Raw Person Names into Structured Components
text: program takes raw text individual names input returns data frame name parsed component parts: SALUTATION FIRST_NAME MIDDLE_NAME LAST_NAME SUFFIX STATUS GENDER GENDER_CONFIDENCE matching done probabilistically based upon frequencies name appearing first name last name US birth certificates. Gender coding similarly done probabilistically using first name parsed string Census data table. parse_name() parses single name returns one-row data frame. Set sanitize = TRUE input still contains punctuation, titles, clutter: parse_names() function utilizes parallelization speed large jobs.
code: x <- 'livingston III,  Mr. MICHAEL JOHN9' parse_name( x, sanitize = TRUE ) #   salutation first_name middle_name  last_name suffix status gender gender_confidence # 1         MR    MICHAEL        JOHN LIVINGSTON    III             M              99.6  x <- "THOMAS H VON KAMECKE" parse_name( x, sanitize = TRUE ) #   salutation first_name middle_name   last_name suffix status gender gender_confidence # 1               THOMAS           H VON-KAMECKE                    M              99.8  x <- c("Karen H Green", "ED MARKS", "MATTHEW BERSHADKER", "R Blincoe",        "HAFER JR EDMUND L AIA", "Dr Leslie Smith", "THOMAS H VON KAMECKE") parse_names(x)                    name salutation first_name middle_name   last_name suffix status gender gender_confidence 1         Karen H Green                 KAREN           H       GREEN                    F               100 2              ED MARKS                    ED                   MARKS                    M               100 3    MATTHEW BERSHADKER               MATTHEW              BERSHADKER                    M              99.7 4             R Blincoe                     R                 BLINCOE                    U              50.0 5 HAFER JR EDMUND L AIA        AIA     EDMUND           L       HAFER     JR             M               100 6       Dr Leslie Smith         DR     LESLIE                   SMITH                    F              66.8 7  THOMAS H VON KAMECKE                THOMAS           H VON-KAMECKE                    M              99.8   # census data table used for name position assignment and gender  head( census.names )       name male_value female_value first_name_value last_name_value 1:     AAB          0            0                0             133 2:  AABERG          0            0                0             469 3:    AABY          0            0                0             220 4: AADLAND          0            0                0             374 5:  AAFEDT          0            0                0             138 6: AAGAARD          0            0                0             300 x <- get_example_names( n=1000 )   start_time <- Sys.time() pn <- parse_names( x ) end_time <- Sys.time()  end_time - start_time # Time difference of 8.7648 secs

title: Known Titles and Abbreviations — known_titles

title: Known Titles and Abbreviations — known_titles
Known Titles and Abbreviations — known_titles
text: tibble three columns: abbr Character abbreviation short form title. label Expanded descriptive form title credential. type Category title (e.g., "Academic Degree", "Military Rank").

title: Known Titles and Abbreviations — known_titles
text: dataset intended use name-parsing, record linkage, entity resolution applications, providing consistent reference recognizing expanding abbreviated titles personal organizational names. type field groups abbreviation broad semantic categories : Personal Title: honorifics like "Mr", "Ms", "Dr". Academic Degree: academic professional degrees (e.g., "PhD", "MD", "MBA"). Religious Title: ecclesiastical clerical designations (e.g., "Rev", "Fr", "Sister"). Civic / Political Title: governmental judicial titles (e.g., "Senator", "Judge", "Honorable"). Military Rank / Affiliation: formal ranks affiliations (e.g., "Lt", "Col", "USAF"). Professional Credential: licensed certified professional credentials (e.g., "CPA", "PE", "RN"). Organizational Role: internal titles positions (e.g., "CEO", "VP", "Ex Officio"). : geographic contextual markers part formal titles (e.g., "La", "ZL").

title: Known Titles and Abbreviations — known_titles
code: titles <- known_titles() dplyr::filter(titles, abbr %in% c("MD", "CPA", "LT")) #> # A tibble: 3 × 3 #>   abbr  label                       type                    #>   <chr> <chr>                       <chr>                   #> 1 MD    Doctor of Medicine          Academic Degree         #> 2 LT    Lieutenant                  Military Rank           #> 3 CPA   Certified Public Accountant Professional Credential  # Lookup utility example title_lookup <- setNames(titles$label, titles$abbr) title_lookup["PHD"] #>                    PHD  #> "Doctor of Philosophy"
